STAGE 1 - constraint extraction (ideation agent, round 3 of the behaviour-graph-curvature line).
GOAL: fix the hard constraints before choosing a coupling position, so the proposal cannot repeat the two measured failures.
READ: the round brief only (no files readable). Key numbers: baseline TIGER_RQ-VAE (247/7414/20223) Stage3 test_recall@10 = 0.055537; round-1 arm spent standardised curvature delta=[-0.328,-0.071,+0.399] on the SID space radius -> codebook collapsed 170->56 distinct triples, recall 0.041888; round-2 CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN entered behaviour as a MULTIPLICATIVE per-pair cost weight and the launch verifier measured margins moving by 1.0 and 3.6 while 0 of 4 argmins moved, and refused it.
OBSERVED: requirement (a) additivity of the behaviour term on the cost, (b) per-level usage multiset exact BY CONSTRUCTION (not a plan whose argmax may miss its marginals), (c) curvature must not act on codebook radius, (d) curvature measured offline / identically on every rank from the training split, standardised against a size-preserving member-shuffle null, (e) three switches in code, only both-on trained.
REASONING: a rescale of a distance only reorders near-equidistant codes, so additivity is not cosmetic - it widens the reorder set from "ratio gap < eps" to "absolute cost gap < bias". And a soft plan is the wrong object: exactness has to be a property of the map from items to labels, i.e. the map must be a composition of label transpositions. That immediately suggests the untried design position: not a radius, not a temperature, not a soft plan, but a QUOTA-PRESERVING PERMUTATION of item->codeword slots. Open: what additive term drives the permutation, and where the measured curvature is spent.

STAGE 2 (final) - answer: EQVOTE-HYP-RQ.
Goal: one implementable mechanism that satisfies (a)-(e). Design: at level l the Euclidean pass defines the QUOTAS q(c) (so usage multiset, distinct-code count 247, and level-1 assignment are exact by construction and cannot collapse); a quota-preserving permutation of item->slot labels is then driven by an ADDITIVE cost S(i,c)=||r_{l-1}(i)-e_c||^2 + lambda_l * (-v(i,c)), where v is the training-successor vote over level-l codewords and every vote is spread by a Poincare kernel exp(-d_P^2/2) evaluated at curvature nu_l=exp(delta_l) on R-normalised codebook coordinates, R = median training content norm (offline). delta_l from the standardised Ollivier curvature of the training behaviour quotient at the baseline SIDs' level-l prefixes vs a 32-draw size-preserving member-shuffle null; shipped as 3 constants, no broadcast. lambda_l = s_l * median reconstruction distortion, s_l = [delta_l]_+ normalised -> [0,0,1] on the measured evidence, so only the fine level (delta_3=+0.399, the level that is MORE tree-like than its null) reallocates; levels 1-2 stay bit-identical to the baseline, which is exactly what protects the 0.079/0.005 first-level hit rates. Exactness lemma: the final label vector is obtained from the Euclidean one by composing label transpositions (swap-local-search), so the multiset is invariant - not argued from marginals. Behaviour off -> v=0 -> all swap gains 0 -> assignment = Euclidean exactly, so frac_top1_changed is measured as 0 vs ~0.15 at level 3 with both on; geometry off -> Euclidean kernel + Euclidean mean -> different votes. Curvature is spent inside the kernel metric only: codebook vectors, quotas and radii are untouched, no radius scale, no soft plan. Cost at frozen scale: only level 3 runs, ~16 MFLOP/step added on 1023x256x32 (2-3x the baseline level-3 assignment), epoch-boundary residual cache 0.4 GFLOP/epoch, offline curvature a few minutes; Stage 2 wall clock ~1.4-2x, Stage 3 untouched.
Status: complete answer printed in the response.
